item.title: Musk says Tesla, SpaceX to build advanced chip manufacturing facility
item.description: Elon Musk says his new Terafab chip plant in Austin aims to produce one terawatt of computing capacity yearly, addressing a critical AI chip shortage.

item.title: Gen Jack Keane ‘highly skeptical’ diplomacy with Iran can achieve military goals
item.description: Gen. Jack Keane warns that a nuclear deal hinges on trust as he remains highly skeptical of U.S.-Iran diplomacy

item.title: Oil giants warn Iran war is inflicting damage 'not only' on energy prices, but the entire global economy
item.description: Oil giants at Houston's CERAWeek warn the U.S.-Israel war with Iran is damaging global supply chains and raising the cost of living worldwide, their executives say.

item.title: Ford recalls more than 254,000 SUVs due to software issues
item.description: Ford is recalling more than 254,000 SUVs in the U.S. after a software defect was found to impact rearview cameras and key driver-assistance safety systems.

item.title: Anduril’s ‘hunter-killer’ drone strategy targets low-cost Iranian threats without high price tags
item.description: Anduril Industries says it can mass-produce low-cost autonomous drones to counter cheap Iranian munitions, replacing costly Cold War-era technology.

item.title: More American workers are struggling than thriving for first time: poll
item.description: A new Gallup poll found that more U.S. workers are struggling than thriving for the first time since the Life Evaluation Index began in 2008.

item.title: Meta ordered to pay $375M after jury finds platform enabled child predators in landmark New Mexico case
item.description: A New Mexico jury ordered Meta to pay $375 million, finding the company misled users about safety and allegedly enabled child sexual exploitation on its platforms.

item.title: JetBlue flight turns back after striking a coyote on the runway: 'We thought it was a joke'
item.description: A JetBlue passenger says she heard a loud thud as Flight 1129 reportedly struck a coyote on the runway at T.F. Green Airport in Rhode Island, forcing the plane to turn back.

item.title: Faster-than-sound passenger flights could soon return to US skies after key House vote
item.description: U.S. air travel could soon go supersonic after the House voted to lift a decades-old restriction on flights faster than the speed of sound, pending Senate approval.

item.title: US bans new foreign-made consumer internet routers over security concerns
item.description: The FCC is banning the import of all new foreign-made consumer routers over cybersecurity concerns amid a broader crackdown on Chinese-made electronic devices.

item.title: Ken Griffey Jr named 'CEO of H2O' as Primo Brands launches healthy hydration campaign for 2026 MLB season
item.description: Baseball legend Ken Griffey Jr. has been named Primo Brands' first-ever "CEO of H2O," leading a national healthy hydration campaign tied to the 2026 MLB season.

item.title: Supreme Court tosses $1B copyright verdict in record companies' battle over illegal internet downloads
item.description: The Supreme Court unanimously ruled Wednesday that internet providers are not liable for copyright infringement by their users, delivering an opinion in Cox v. Sony and tossing a $1 billion verdict.

item.title: Toyota recalls more than 144,000 Lexus vehicles over rearview camera failure risk
item.description: Toyota recalls over 144,000 Lexus vehicles over a rearview camera defect tied to a software issue that may increase crash risk, regulators said.

item.title: MLB All-Star Alex Bregman joins Patrick Mahomes, Breanna Stewart as Throne SPORT COFFEE partner
item.description: Chicago Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman invested in Throne SPORT COFFEE, joining Patrick Mahomes and Breanna Stewart ahead of MLB Opening Day.

item.title: ‘Conditions for a labor market crisis’: Rising care costs push women out of workforce
item.description: Catalyst research shows that rigid work structures and caregiving costs drove nearly 455,000 women from U.S. jobs within seven months in 2025, raising fears of a labor shortage.
